description:
Trigger: AddressBook/set with onSuccessSetIsDefault set to a number, boolean, array, or object value (any non-string, non-null).

Bad behavior: addressbook.rs:383 has '_ => {} // malformed — silently ignored'. The set call succeeds with no signal back to the client that the argument was malformed and the default was not changed.

This silent-drop diverges from the handler's own treatment of the destroy array (lines 247-255): a non-string element there returns JmapError::invalid_arguments. The /set destroy and onSuccessSetIsDefault arguments are both Id-typed in the spec; their malformed-type handling should be consistent.

RFC 9610 §2.3 says ON SUCCESS: 'If the id is not found or if the change is not permitted by the server for policy reasons, it MUST be ignored.' That justifies silent-drop for 'id not found' or 'policy refused', but the spec language is about the *value* being a valid Id that the server can't act on. A non-string TYPE is a different failure mode — it's an invalidArguments-shaped failure, not a §2.3 silent-ignore.

The current test set_on_success_set_is_default_bad_type_ignored at addressbook.rs:546-562 ENSHRINES the silent-drop behavior as correct. That test should be inverted: a malformed onSuccessSetIsDefault should return invalidArguments (or, less aggressively, surface an error in notUpdated against a synthetic id).

This is a maintainer-burden issue: future contributors will look at the test, follow the pattern, and write more silent-drop-on-malformed handlers. The class of bug is the same as the Pattern G sweep that closed across the workspace (JMAP-q2wa.1, vacation.rs JMAP-j7pa.1, etc.).
title: onSuccessSetIsDefault malformed-type handling silently drops the request — diverges from /set destroy non-string rejection
